description: Renovate keeps the three vendored rulesets in maisecrets/rules/ current. It runs as the scheduled job `renovate` in .gitlab-ci.yml, self-hosted, because only a self-hosted Renovate runs postUpgradeTasks.

A bump of a *_VERSION file alone would leave the JSON the detector reads at the old version (red: tests/test_vendored_rules.py). The postUpgradeTasks run the sync script of that ruleset, so one MR carries the version and the regenerated rules together.

The sync scripts read the upstream rules as data (scripts/_static_python.py) and execute no upstream code; the job holds one credential, the Renovate token, a Developer token. Nothing merges by itself: a person merges the tested MR.
Only the custom managers are on: the CI images and the GitHub Actions stay pinned by hand.

customManagers.description: gitleaks: the rules come from config/gitleaks.toml at the release tag
detect-secrets: the keyword and basic-auth regexes at the release tag
Presidio: the pattern recognizers of the presidio-analyzer package

packageRules.description: One commit subject the release job reads: `deps(rules): ...` is a patch release with a Dependencies line in the changelog
A major release can change the rule format
